name: Wolf
description: Coordinated pursuit predation with specialized roles (driver, flanker, ambusher) via real-time gaze and postural communication. Dynamic context-dependent hierarchy. Howl harmonics encode identity and location across 16 km. Trophic cascade restructures ecosystems.

core_attributes.neurology: highly developed prefrontal cortex, mirror neuron system
core_attributes.pattern: coordinated pursuit, dynamic social hierarchy, acoustic identity encoding, trophic cascade

scope.definition: Probability of successful prey capture per hunt initiation when a pack of ≥4 wolves employs relay-chase coordination, compared to 0.15 for lone wolves targeting same prey size.

evidence.source: Mech & Boitani (2003) 'Wolves: Behavior, Ecology, and Conservation', Univ. Chicago Press; Peterson & Ciucci (2003) predation success analysis across 3 pack studies.
cross_domain_examples: Yellowstone pack relay-chase success rate 0.30 vs lone wolf 0.05 for elk
coordinated surround tactics observed in African wild dogs (convergent evolution, 0.85 success)
dolphin cooperative herding of fish schools: analogous spatial role assignment

scope.falsifiability: If coordinated wolf packs show no statistically significant higher success than lone wolves over 200+ documented hunts, role-division coordination is not the causal factor.
scope.measurement_limits: Success rates vary by prey type, terrain, and pack experience. Deep snow favors wolves; shallow terrain favors prey. Pack size beyond 8 shows diminishing returns.

scope.definition: Classification accuracy of individual wolf identity from howl spectrogram features (fundamental frequency, modulation rate, harmonic ratios) by trained convolutional classifiers, used as proxy for wolf perceptual discrimination.

evidence.source: Frommolt et al. (2003) 'Acoustic monitoring of wolves', Bioacoustics 13:255-270; Theberge & Falls (1967) 'Howling as a means of communication in timber wolves', American Zoologist 7:331-338.
cross_domain_examples: individual wolf howl ID accuracy 0.89-0.95 in spectral analysis studies
humans identify individual voices by voice signature at 0.94 accuracy
seismic monitoring of individual elephants by footfall signature: analogous identity encoding

scope.falsifiability: If howl spectral features are shown not to encode individual identity (through playback experiments showing wolves cannot distinguish familiar from unfamiliar howls), the identity-encoding function fails.
scope.measurement_limits: Acoustic identity degrades over distances >10 km and in dense forest. Seasonal hormonal changes alter fundamental frequency, potentially degrading identity signal.

scope.definition: Proportional reduction in riparian overgrazing index (plant biomass recovery rate) following wolf reintroduction into an ungulate-dominated ecosystem, averaged across Yellowstone and analogous reintroduction studies.

evidence.source: Ripple & Beschta (2012) 'Trophic cascades in Yellowstone', Biological Conservation 150:70-79; Fortin et al. (2005) 'Wolves influence elk movements', Ecology 86:1320-1330.
cross_domain_examples: Yellowstone riparian willow/aspen recovery 0.65-0.92 after wolf reintroduction (Ripple 2012)
Isle Royale wolf-moose-balsam fir trophic cascade 50-year documentation
Scandinavia: moose browsing pressure reduced 40% in wolf territories vs control areas
sea otter removal → urchin explosion → kelp forest collapse: analogous apex predator cascade

scope.falsifiability: If plant community recovery in wolf reintroduction zones is statistically identical to control zones after 10 years, behavioral landscape of fear (not direct predation) is not the mechanism.
scope.measurement_limits: Trophic cascade magnitude depends on prey density, alternative prey availability, and human hunting pressure on wolves. The Yellowstone result may overestimate typical cascade strength.
